content:
Grace Kim: can someone grab Nsight Systems traces for the top 3 “mystery” cases from today’s matrix? need kernel timeline + launch overhead to confirm if this is real or scheduler interaction.

Targets (please keep the exact args so we can diff apples-to-apples):
1) H100 / Model: `rmx-llama-70b` / workload: `prefill-heavy` (p50 prompt ~1.5k, gen 256) / mode: `fp8_attn=on, int8_mm=off` → TTFT regression
2) H100 / Model: `rmx-mistral-7b` / workload: `decode-heavy` (prompt 256, gen 1024) / mode: `int8_mm=on` → TPOT not improving despite microbench win
3) A100 / Model: `rmx-llama-13b` / workload: `mixed` (suite v3 “prod_mix”, conc=16) / mode: `fp8_attn=on` → variance spike

If you can, please upload:
- `.qdrep` + `.nsys-rep`
- `nsys stats` output (gpukernsum + cudaapisum)
- the benchmark runner JSON artifact for the run (includes SHA/CUDA/driver/clocks)

Owners (tentative):
- Case (1): @Isabella Rossi
- Case (2): @Yuki Sato
- Case (3): @Marcus Reed

Command template (edit the `--case-id` + args only):
```bash
# on the benchmark node (same container as harness)
export RW_BENCH_ARTIFACT_ROOT="/tmp/rw_artifacts"
export RW_BENCH_CASE_ID="nsys_2026-04-16_case1_h100_llama70b_fp8attn"

# keep capture short; we only need steady-state region
nsys profile \
  -t cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --sample=none \
  --cpuctxsw=true \
  --cuda-memory-usage=true \
  --gpu-metrics-device=all \
  --capture-range=nvtx \
  --capture-range-end=stop \
  -o "${RW_BENCH_ARTIFACT_ROOT}/${RW_BENCH_CASE_ID}" \
  --force-overwrite=true \
  -- \
  ./rw-bench run \
    --suite top-hosted-models-benchmark-suite-v3 \
    --gpu h100 \
    --model rmx-llama-70b \
    --workload prefill-heavy \
    --concurrency 8 \
    --kernel-mode fp8_attn \
    --disable-int8-mm

# stats (attach to thread)
nsys stats "${RW_BENCH_ARTIFACT_ROOT}/${RW_BENCH_CASE_ID}.nsys-rep" --report gpukernsum,cudaapisum > "${RW_BENCH_ARTIFACT_ROOT}/${RW_BENCH_CASE_ID}_stats.txt"
```
Artifact upload:
- `gs://rw-benchmark-artifacts/fp8-int8-sprint/nsys/2026-04-16/<case-id>/`
- and paste the gs:// link back here + add it to the matrix row Notes

Ping me if the NVTX capture range isn’t triggering; we can flip to duration-based but would rather keep it tight.

(reactions: :eyes:2)

Rina Kobayashi: FYI harness already drops NVTX markers around steady-state region if you pass `--profile-mode nsys`. it wraps warmup separately.

If you’re using benchlab runner (preferred):
```bash
benchlab matrix run \
  --matrix fp8_int8_v1 \
  --case "h100/llama70b/prefill-heavy/fp8_attn" \
  --nsys \
  --nsys-capture nvtx \
  --artifact-gcs "gs://rw-benchmark-artifacts/fp8-int8-sprint/nsys/2026-04-16/" \
  --tag "trace_req_1776425512"
```
It will upload automatically + print the link.

Isabella Rossi: taking case (1). i can run on `rt-h100-usw2-bench-03` after my current calibration job finishes (~20m). will keep clocks locked (same as matrix runs).

Hiro Tanaka: +1 on keeping it consistent: same image as matrix runner (`runtime-bench:1.22.0-rc3`), don’t upgrade nsys locally. we saw different overhead w/ nsys 2026.1 vs 2025.4.

Also please make sure these env vars are set (runner usually does it):
```bash
export CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS=1
export NVIDIA_TF32_OVERRIDE=0
```
Not strictly required for tracing but avoids accidental config drift.

Yuki Sato: i’ll take case (2). question: do we want `--trace=cublas` too? last time it blew up file size.

Grace Kim: for (2) just `cuda,nvtx,osrt` is fine. we mainly need kernel launch cadence + stream syncs. if we suspect cublasLt heuristics we can re-run w/ extra traces.

Marcus Reed: ok i can do case (3) but i’m blocked on A100 node allocation until 6pm. can someone confirm which cluster to use? don’t want to hit shared capacity.

Julian Moore: use `rt-a100-use1-bench-02` (dedicated bench partition). Irene set aside 2 nodes for us tonight. avoid `prod-a100-*`.

Marcus Reed: got it.

Isabella Rossi: update: ran case (1) once, NVTX capture worked. uploading now.
`gs://rw-benchmark-artifacts/fp8-int8-sprint/nsys/2026-04-16/nsys_2026-04-16_case1_h100_llama70b_fp8attn/`
Stats snippet (full txt in bucket):
```text
Top GPU kernels by total time:
  fp8_attention_fwd_kernel<hs=8192,hd=128>  31.8%
  rmsnorm_fused                             10.4%
  rope_apply                                8.9%
CUDA API summary:
  cudaLaunchKernel   44.2%
  cudaMemcpyAsync    7.1%
  cudaStreamWaitEvent 6.5%
```
Big thing: tons of short launches during prefill; looks like we’re not batching prefill as much w/ fp8 attn path (?)

Grace Kim: :thumbsup: thanks. the `cudaLaunchKernel` % is exactly what i was worried about.

Yuki Sato: case (2) done + uploaded:
`gs://rw-benchmark-artifacts/fp8-int8-sprint/nsys/2026-04-16/nsys_2026-04-16_case2_h100_mistral7b_int8mm/`
Quick read: int8 matmul kernel is faster per call but we’re getting extra dequant/reformat kernels between layers (maybe alignment path?). will dig w/ ncu next if needed.

Hiro Tanaka: that “reformat” is likely the fallback pack kernel if K not multiple of 64. check shape guardrails in `pr-19841` vs model config.

Marcus Reed: case (3) running now on `rt-a100-use1-bench-02`. ETA 25m.

Marcus Reed: uploaded case (3):
`gs://rw-benchmark-artifacts/fp8-int8-sprint/nsys/2026-04-16/nsys_2026-04-16_case3_a100_llama13b_prod_mix_fp8attn/`
Observations: GPU timeline shows periodic gaps aligned with scheduler queue drain; looks more like host-side jitter + backpressure than kernel variance. might correlate w/ queue depth spikes we saw in `pr-19855` metrics.

Grace Kim: perfect. i’ll link these into the matrix + open a follow-up task:
- investigate prefill batching window interaction w/ fp8 attention (launch overhead)
- check int8 pack/reformat path on mistral7b (shape guard or layout)
- scheduler jitter on a100 prod_mix (queue depth + backpressure)

Thanks all. (reactions: :pray:3)
